query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a chromium-rich coating to boride-based components can improve their resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion.
generation.conditions: Temperature below 700°C and exposure to molten aluminum
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective chromium oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The chromium-rich coating reacts with oxygen to form a protective chromium oxide layer, which prevents the molten aluminum from coming into contact with the boride-based component and corroding it.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion compared to uncoated boride-based components
generation.boundary: Temperature above 700°C or exposure to other corrosive substances
generation.uncertainty: The effectiveness of the chromium-rich coating in improving resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion may vary depending on the specific composition and microstructure of the boride-based component and the coating.

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled laboratory experiment with coated and uncoated boride-based components exposed to molten aluminum under controlled temperature conditions
measurements: Microstructural analysis of the coating and the component
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated boride-based components show no significant improvement in resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion compared to the uncoated components, the hypothesis is falsified.
